title: Computation of unbounded derived morphisms on arbitrary K-injective resolutions
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] and $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ an additive functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Write $K(\mathcal A)$ for complexes modulo chain homotopy and $Q_{\mathcal A}:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and similarly for $\mathcal B$. Assume every complex of $\mathcal A$ has a K-injective resolution, meaning a quasi-isomorphism to a complex $I$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(E,I)=0$ for every acyclic $E$. Let $(RF,\eta)$ be the unbounded total right derived functor [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], with unit $\eta_N:Q_{\mathcal B}(FN)\to RF(Q_{\mathcal A}N)$. For a K-injective resolution $a:N\to I$, set
$$c_a=\eta_I^{-1}\circ RF(Q_{\mathcal A}a):RF(Q_{\mathcal A}N)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{\mathcal B}(FI).$$
For complexes $N,N'$, any morphism $h:Q_{\mathcal A}N\to Q_{\mathcal A}N'$ in the derived category, and K-injective resolutions $a:N\to I$, $b:N'\to J$, there is a unique homotopy class $g:I\to J$ with
$$Q_{\mathcal A}g=(Q_{\mathcal A}b)\circ h\circ(Q_{\mathcal A}a)^{-1},$$
and
$$c_b\circ RF(h)\circ c_a^{-1}=Q_{\mathcal B}(Fg).$$
Here $Fg$ means degreewise application of $F$ to any representative of that homotopy class. These formulas are compatible with identities and composition of derived morphisms. For another resolution $a':N\to I'$, the canonical transition $c_{a'}c_a^{-1}$ is $Q_{\mathcal B}(Fk)$ for the unique homotopy class $k:I\to I'$ satisfying $Q_{\mathcal A}k=Q_{\mathcal A}a'(Q_{\mathcal A}a)^{-1}$; these transitions are isomorphisms, satisfy the cocycle identity for three resolutions, and intertwine the displayed formula for every $h$.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined): K-injective computation of total right derived functors; the stated arbitrary-resolution/naturality consequence is an agent formulation of this computation, not a verbatim Stacks lemma.

proof.text: Use the homotopy-category functor $F_K$ of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. This is independent of the chosen representative: if $u-v=d s+s d$, additivity gives $F(u)-F(v)=F(d)F(s)+F(s)F(d)$, so $F(s)$ is a homotopy. Functoriality degree by degree gives $F_K(vu)=F_K(v)F_K(u)$ and $F_K(1)=1$. Thus $Q_{\mathcal B}(Fg)$ is well-defined on a homotopy class.

The unit of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] has invertible components $\eta_I$ on every K-injective $I$. The localization $Q_{\mathcal A}$ inverts the quasi-isomorphism $a:N\to I$, and the functor $RF$ preserves isomorphisms. Consequently $c_a=\eta_I^{-1}RF(Q_{\mathcal A}a)$ is an isomorphism with inverse $RF((Q_{\mathcal A}a)^{-1})\eta_I$. The same applies to $b$ and to every other resolution in the statement.

source.place: Tags 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined) and 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies): computing unit on K-injectives

proof.text: Put $t=(Q_{\mathcal A}b)h(Q_{\mathcal A}a)^{-1}:Q_{\mathcal A}I\to Q_{\mathcal A}J$. Since $J$ is K-injective, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] applied with source $I$ and target $J$ says that $Q_{\mathcal A}:\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(I,J)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(Q_{\mathcal A}I,Q_{\mathcal A}J)$ is bijective. Its surjectivity gives the required $g$ with $Q_{\mathcal A}g=t$, and its injectivity gives uniqueness.

Naturality of the unit in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] on the homotopy class $g:I\to J$ gives $RF(Q_{\mathcal A}g)\eta_I=\eta_J Q_{\mathcal B}(Fg)$. Using the preceding equation for $Q_{\mathcal A}g$, functoriality and the inverse computed in step 2 gives directly $$c_b RF(h)c_a^{-1}=\eta_J^{-1}RF((Q_{\mathcal A}b)h(Q_{\mathcal A}a)^{-1})\eta_I=\eta_J^{-1}RF(Q_{\mathcal A}g)\eta_I=Q_{\mathcal B}(Fg).$$

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined), unit naturality; agent-written explicit calculation

proof.text: For the identity derived morphism with the same resolution at both ends, its transported target is $1_{Q_{\mathcal A}I}$, whose unique representative is $1_I$. For $h:Q_{\mathcal A}N\to Q_{\mathcal A}N^{\prime}$ and $h^{\prime}:Q_{\mathcal A}N^{\prime}\to Q_{\mathcal A}N^{\prime\prime}$ use resolutions $a,b,d$ and representatives $g,g^{\prime}$. Then $$Q_{\mathcal A}(g^{\prime}g)=(Q_{\mathcal A}d)h^{\prime}(Q_{\mathcal A}b)^{-1}(Q_{\mathcal A}b)h(Q_{\mathcal A}a)^{-1}=(Q_{\mathcal A}d)(h^{\prime}h)(Q_{\mathcal A}a)^{-1}.$$ Injectivity in [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] makes $g^{\prime}g$ the representative of $h^{\prime}h$. The functors $F_K$ and $Q_{\mathcal B}$ preserve these identities and composites, proving compatibility of the formula.

source.place: Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective), uniqueness of representatives; elementary identity and composition calculation

proof.text: Apply steps 3 and 4 to $h=1_{Q_{\mathcal A}N}$ with resolutions $a$ and $a^{\prime}$. They give the unique $k:I\to I^{\prime}$ with $Q_{\mathcal A}k=(Q_{\mathcal A}a^{\prime})(Q_{\mathcal A}a)^{-1}$ and the transition formula $T_{a^{\prime},a}:=c_{a^{\prime}}c_a^{-1}=Q_{\mathcal B}(Fk)$. Each transition is invertible, with inverse $T_{a,a^{\prime}}$, because both $c$ maps are invertible. For a third resolution, cancellation gives $$T_{a^{\prime\prime},a^{\prime}}T_{a^{\prime},a}=c_{a^{\prime\prime}}c_{a^{\prime}}^{-1}c_{a^{\prime}}c_a^{-1}=T_{a^{\prime\prime},a}.$$ This also gives the identity transition when the two resolutions coincide.

source.place: Tags 070I and 070Y, consequence of the preceding representative and unit calculations

proof.text: For alternative resolutions $a^{\prime}$ of $N$ and $b^{\prime}$ of $N^{\prime}$, let $M_{b,a}(h)=c_bRF(h)c_a^{-1}$. Then $$T_{b^{\prime},b}M_{b,a}(h)=c_{b^{\prime}}RF(h)c_a^{-1}=M_{b^{\prime},a^{\prime}}(h)T_{a^{\prime},a}.$$ By step 4 the two $M$ maps are exactly the images $Q_{\mathcal B}(Fg)$ for the respective unique homotopy classes. This explicit commutative square proves that the transitions intertwine the displayed formula for every derived morphism, completing all clauses.
